senses.gloss: (transitive, now, _, rare) To summarise. [from 15th c.]
(transitive) To create a makeshift, ad hoc solution from resources at hand.
(transitive) To put together.
(transitive) Cause to become one; make into a unit; consolidate; merge; combine.
(transitive) To epitomize something by expressing it as a brief summary.
(ambitransitive) To summarize or repeat in concise form.
(transitive) To join together; to unite; to combine.
In or to all locations under discussion.

That or those belonging to me.
Abbreviation of minimum.
Of a person, preferring the customs of earlier times and the old-style ways.
At an important, elevated, or exalted level in a hierarchy or organization; high-level.
To express approval (of something) by clapping the hands.

One of four seasons, traditionally the second, marked by the longest and typically hottest days of the year due to the inclination of the Earth and thermal lag. Typically regarded as spanning either the period between the summer solstice to the autumnal equinox, or the months of June, July, and August in the Northern Hemisphere and the months of December, January and February in the Southern Hemisphere.
Relating to the summer.
The ordinal form of the number sixteen.
In the parts of this document, statement, or book that follow; after this
Assured by or of one's self; confident in one's own abilities.
Any of several species of trees of the genus Aesculus.
A recording or medium of visual content, especially audiovisual content for playback; a motion picture, movie, film.
A relatively wide magnetic tape used for recording visual images and sounds (as of a television production) for subsequent playback or broadcasting.
(colloquial, countable, uncountable) Abbreviation of television.
(transitive) To convey or communicate; to make known or explicit.
To express (an action, thought or idea) by means of particular words.
One who, or that which, achieves assumed goals.
Resulting in success; assuring or promoting success; accomplishing what was proposed; having the desired effect.
Having many accomplishments, often as a result of study or training.
In a happy or cheerful manner; with happiness.
To have (as an effect).
To cause or produce (a given result); to bring about (a given result).
To set off an event or action; to bring about; to produce.
Data fed into a process with the intention of it shaping or affecting the output of that process.
The art or science of cultivating the ground, including the growing and harvesting of crops, and the rearing and management of livestock.
Of or pertaining to rural, agricultural employment; often contrasted with urban blue-collar employment.
The occupation or work of a husbandman or farmer; the cultivation of crops and the raising of livestock; agriculture.
animal
(formal) Any of certain extant canids regarded as similar to the dog or wolf (including coyotes, jackals, etc.) but distinguished from the vulpines, which are regarded as fox-like.
A dog.
A mean, worthless fellow; a rascal; a villain; a person without honor or virtue.
Within a short time; quickly.
In or after a short time; soon.
Before long; soon. [from 15thc.]
Soon; in a little while.
A single droplet of rainwater that has just fallen or is falling from the sky.

Money or goods collected by a government (or an entity to whom the government has delegated this power, e.g. in tax farming) to fund itself and its services, for example by levying a charge on income, purchases (sales), property or harvest, other than that money which is collected by the government in exchange for specific goods (e.g. the purchase of surplus vehicles).
(chiefly, _, historical) A tax, tariff or duty that is imposed, especially on merchandise.
Happening or occurring during daylight, or primarily active during that time.
Without end, eternal.
Unchanged through time or space; permanent.
Persisting for an extended period of time.
to mend or repair
To restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition; to mend; to remedy.
to bring back to a previous condition or state
To physically repair (something that is broken, defaced, decayed, torn, or otherwise damaged).
To fiddle with something in an attempt to fix, mend or improve it, especially in an experimental or unskilled manner.
fine, dry particles
The fine particles which are the result of reducing a dry substance by pounding, grinding, or triturating, or the result of decay; dust.
Any particle that has been removed by a file or similar implement; a shaving.
The person who manages the performers in a circus ring.
Of or pertaining to numbers.
One of various species of grass of the genus Cymbopogon, especially Cymbopogon citratus, which have a lemon-like taste and aroma, and are used in cooking, for tea, and for fragrance.
The chaffinch.
One who is in charge or something.
The head cook of a restaurant or other establishment.
A person who conducts an orchestra, choir or other music ensemble; a professional whose occupation is conducting.
(music) The conductor of a musical ensemble, especially a brass or military band.
(astrology) The zodiac sign for the scorpion, ruled by Mars and covering October 23 - November 22 (tropical astrology) or November 16 - December 15 (sidereal astrology).
(constellation) A constellation of the zodiac, roughly shaped like a scorpion. Its brightest star is the red giant Antares.
The starting point of a logical deduction or thought; basis.
A regulation, law, guideline.
The base or foot of a column, statue, vase, lamp.
A basis or foundation.
(military) Airhead, beachhead, bridgehead, lodgement.
A slightly curved but almost flat dish from which food is served or eaten.
A vessel such as a plate for holding or serving food, often flat with a depressed region in the middle.
An object round and gently curved, shaped like a saucer.
The quantity contained on a plate.
An anglerfish, Lophius piscatorius.
Any large bottom-dwelling anglerfish of the genus Lophius, such as Lophius piscatorius, of the Atlantic, having a large head and mouth.
Any fish of the bony fish order Lophiiformes, which have an outgrowth they wiggle to lure and catch their prey.
Happening by chance.
(zodiac constellations) A constellation of the zodiac traditionally taken to represent the pair of twins Castor and Pollux in Greek mythology. It contains the stars Castor, Pollux, and Alhena.
An area in which land mines or naval mines have been laid.
Any of various logic-based computer games in which the player has to discover the position of mines in a rectangular grid, based on numerical hints.
(uncountable) An amorphous movement of right-wing white nationalists opposed to multiculturalism and egalitarianism by race and sex, mostly active on the Internet.
Improper; unfit; unsuitable.
A venue where sporting events are held.
A unit of distance equal to one-eighth of a mile (220 yards, or 201.168 metres), now mainly used in measuring distances in farmland and horse racing.
Any one of the several stages of postembryonic development which an arthropod undergoes, between molts, before it reaches sexual maturity.
(historical) A Greek unit of distance based on standardized footraces, equivalent to about 185.4 metres.
Cause, interest or account.
A reason or excuse; a motive; a persuasion.
(translation studies) The function of a written or spoken text, especially in the context of translating and interpreting.
Anhydrous: free from or lacking water in any state, regardless of the presence of other liquids.
In a cordial, warm, friendly or heartfelt manner.
Agreement; harmony; conformity; compliance.
The state, quality, or the fact of being eligible.
(telecommunication) the capability of two or more items or components of equipment or material to exist or function in the same system or environment without mutual interference.
To correspond, concur, or agree.
The quality of being suitable.
Suitability; the quality of being apt or suitable.
Frightened; filled with terror.
Any of various succulent plants of the Crassulaceae family, native to temperate zones, especially in genus Sedum
Demanding silence.
To depict someone or something a particular way (often negative).
The state of things; condition; predicament; impasse.
The status or condition of something
A body position, typically associated with the practice of yoga.
Any of a certain family of trick-taking card games.
To start to operate.
To ride in a boat, especially a sailboat.
A slippery secretion from the lining of the mucous membranes.
Mucus, especially mucus from the nose.
A piece of solid or semisolid mucus in or removed from a nostril.
Nasal mucus; snot.
(biblical) The twentieth book of the New Testament of the Bible, the general epistle of James.
(Mormonism) The fifth son of Lehi and one of the younger brothers of Nephi, author of one of the books in the Book of Mormon.
Any of the genus Trichuris of roundworms that infect certain mammals
A magnetic tape that stores analog sound for later playback on a tape player.
Someone who intentionally kills a person, especially a professional who kills a public or political figure.
A religious leader in Twelverism.
(hormone) Pertaining to hormones.
Daytime supervision, usually of children or pets.
Live entertainment held in a restaurant or nightclub; the genre of music associated with this form of entertainment, especially in early 20th century Europe.
Someone who sleeps.
A sleepy person.
A flat-faced fulling hammer.
An object so suspended inside a bell that it may hit the bell and cause it to ring; a clanger or tongue.
A wooden mallet, used by a courtroom judge, or by a committee chairman, struck against a sounding block to quieten those present, or by an auctioneer to accept the highest bid at auction.
A circular device attached to a door, the rotation of which permits the unlatching of the door.
A club-shaped, round-headed stick used in a mortar to pound, crush, rub or grind things.
To make a bluff; to give the impression that one’s hand is stronger than it is.
A device capable of registering a specific substance or physical phenomenon, and that optionally sounds an alarm or triggers a warning.
(geology) The Ordovician period.
A country consisting of around 340 islands in Micronesia, in Oceania. Official name: Republic of Palau. Capital: Ngerulmud.
A state of the United States.
(informal) A system of vessels or ducts in the human body, especially the genitourinary system.
Relating to the intestines.
The internal organs of a human or animal; especially viscera, intestines.
Collectively, the internal organs of the body, especially those contained within the abdominal and thoracic cavities, such as the liver, heart, or stomach.
A wet-cell storage battery.
A person who climbs mountains for sport or pleasure.
A word or phrase that is created by rearranging the letters of another word or phrase.
(sometimes, derogatory, colloquial) A timid, unassertive or cowardly person.
(chiefly, derogatory, slang) Someone who lacks confidence or courage, is weak, ineffectual, irresolute and wishy-washy.
(slang, mildly, derogatory) A weak, ineffectual, cowardly, or timid person.
A small passerine bird (songbird) of the genus Parus or the family Paridae.
Any small passerine bird mostly of the genus Baeolophus, which are found in the woods of the Northern Hemisphere and of Africa.
Of a boy or man, exhibiting behavior or mannerisms considered typical of a woman or unmasculine.
race; ethnicity (in the sense of classification of human beings).
(nautical) A small fleet of warships (usually of the same class), or a fleet of small ships.
Characterised by bloodshed.
Thirsty for blood: inexorably violent or eager for bloodshed; murderous.
The first child to be born to a parent or family.
To apply a force to (an object) such that it moves away from the person or thing applying the force.
Overpowering, staggering, or irresistibly strong.

Any of several species of generalist predatory carnivores in the family Herpestidae; the various species range in size from rats to large cats. Indian mongooses are predators of venomous snakes, though other mongoose species have similar habits.
A tropical fruit of the tree genus Garcinia.
An Egyptian mongoose (Herpestes ichneumon), found in Africa and southern Europe.
place
A piece of currency, usually metallic and in the shape of a disc, but sometimes polygonal, or with a hole in the middle.
The transference of a bodily function or disease to another part of the body, specifically the development of a secondary area of disease remote from the original site, as with some cancers.
An abnormal condition of a human, animal or plant that causes discomfort or dysfunction; distinct from injury insofar as the latter is usually instantaneously acquired.
To (usually temporarily) expel a user from a MUD or similar system
A long, slender, chiefly terrestrial amphibian of the order Caudata, superficially resembling a lizard.
Only partially conscious and aware; confused, groggy.
Slowed or weakened, as by drink, sleepiness, etc.
Queasy, dizzy, or disoriented.
Chaotic, disordered, confused; also, incoherent, rambling.
Neither fully conscious nor unconscious, partially aware but confused or distracted.
(Christianity) In Christian belief, the three persons of the Godhead: the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit.

To restrain someone; to arrest.
